caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 2013 with Civil Rule No. 78(FM) of 2013.
lawyer:
Khair Ezaz Maswood, Advocate ---------- For the Defendant-Opposite-Party-Appellant. 
Abul Kalam Chowdhury, Advocate ------------- For the Third Parties-Petitioners-Respondents Nos.1-6. 
Md Imam Hasan with Md Shahinul Islam, Advocates --------------- For the Plaintiff-Opposite-Party-Respondent No.7.
parties:
Shamsul Alam (Md) -------- Defendant-Opposite-Party-Appellant
VS
Md Liyakat Ullah and others ---------- Third Parties-Petitioners-Respondents
full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J : This first miscellaneous appeal has been filed on 16-7-2012 by the defendant No.2 opposite-party against the judgment and order dated 3-5-2012 passed by the learned Judge-in-charge, Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka allowing the Miscellaneous Case No.14 of 2009 filed under section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 read with Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure releasing the case property from attachment in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 13 of 2008.

2. The said miscellaneous appeal was filed without depositing the statutory deposit as contemplated under section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred as the Ain). Subsequently, the appellant filed an application on 16-7-2012 for dispensing the statutory deposit for filing appeal against the order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat.

3. This court by order dated 28-11-2012 admit the appeal on the ground that the appellant filed the instant appeal not challenging the decree in question nor controverting the demand or claim of the bank rather supporting the claim of the bank. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the appellant was permitted to prefer this appeal without any statutory deposit as contemplated under section 41 of the Ain, 2003 provisionally.

4. Then the appeal was registered as FMA No. 11 of 2013 on 8-1-2013. Subsequently, Civil Rule No. 78(FM) of 2013 was issued on 22-1-2013 calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 3-5-2012 passed by the learned Judge-in-Charge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 2009 should not be stayed till disposal of First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 2013.

5. Pending hearing of the rule, let the operation of the impugned judgment and order dated 3-5-2012 passed by the learned Judge-in-Charge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 2009 as well as the further proceeding of the Artha Rin Execution Case No. 13 of 2008 be stayed for a period of 4 months from date.

6. Respondent Nos. 1-6 Third-party-claiment appeared in the appeal through their learned Advocate Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhury on 26-11-2013. Mr Md Imam Hasan, learned Advocate appeared in this appeal on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent No. 7-Bank on 22-5-2013.

7. Third party respondent Nos. 1-6 contested the said application for dispensing with the statutory deposit by filing counter affidavit dated 27-5-2013 stating, inter alia, that the miscellaneous appeal arises against the judgment and order dated 3-5-2012 passed by the learned Judge-in-Charge, Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No.14 of 2009 which was filed under section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 read with Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The aforesaid miscellaneous case arises out of Artha Rin Execution Case No. 13 of 2008 for executing the decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No.112 of 2007. Hence provision of section 41(2) of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 which provides mandatory deposit before filing any appeal which is equally applicable in the present appeal.

8. During pendency of the appeal the appellant took additional ground by filing an application under Order XLI, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Previously the matter was heard by another Division Bench of this court after hearing on several occasions learned Advocate of both the parties expressed their opinion and prayed that it would be just and fair to call for the LCR in the instant appeal. Accordingly this court by modifying the order of admission dated 28-11-2012 directed to transmit the Lower Court Records of Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 2009 now lying in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka.

9. Some facts, in short, necessary for the disposal of the present appeal which reads as under:

That the present respondent Nos. 1-6 as Third-party petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 2009 filed under section 32 Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 read with Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure for releasing the case property from attachment in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 13 of 2008 arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 112 of 2007 filed by the plaintiff-respondent No.7, Rupali Bank against the present appeallant-defendant No.2 judgment debtor.

10. The facts of the case as stated in the Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 2009 stated as follows:

That one Jion Box was owner of 0'58 acres land of CS plot No. 5159 and 0'20 acres of CS plot No. 5159/5351 in all 0'78 acres of CS Khatian No. 1704 of Mouja Matuail including other lands; that said Jion Box died leaving one sons Sayedur Rahman, 4 daughters Alesa Khatun, Khairer Nessa, Kulsum Bibi and Anwara Begum; that by amicable partition with sisters Sayedur Rahman became absolute owner and was in exclusive possession in said 0.78 acres land and accordingly it was recorded in his name in SA Khatian No. 2034; that 0.58 acres land of CS and SA plot No. 5159 was recorded in RS plot No. 7460 and 0'20 acres land of CS and SA plot No. 5159/5351 was recorded in RS plot No. 7459 in RS Khatian No. 1467 in the name of said Sayedur Rahman. There was partition deed No. 2478 dated 9-3-1979 between Sayedur Rahman and his sisters. As per said partition deed, Khairer Nessa and Alesa Khatun got other lands which they sold to others by registered Saf-Kabola. Being exclusive and absolute owner and in exclusive possession in aforesaid 0.78 acres Sayedur Rahman sold 0.15 acres of said 2 plots to respondent No. 1 vide registered Saf-Kabola No. 6265 dated 12-11-1980 and also sold 0.15 acres on the same date vide registered Khatian No. 6266 to Md Abdullah father of respondent No. 1 and delivered possession of it. Out of said purchased 0.30 acres 10 acres are in the Southern side of CS and SA plot No. 5159/5351 corresponding RS plot No. 7459 and 0.20 acres of the southern side of CS and -SA plot No. 5159 corresponding RS 7460. It may be mentioned that RS plot No. 7460 and 7459 are in paralal line i.e. side by side and purchased 0.30 acres lands of respondents were in the southern side in one compact i.e. 0.20 acres of RS plot No. 7460 and 0.10 acres of RS plot No. 7459. Respondent No. 1 and his father Abdullah after their purchase developed their purchased 0.30 acres by filling earth, constructed boundary wall and also constructed temporary structures on it. They opened separate mutation Khatian No. 2034/2 and holding No. 3901 in the name of respondent No. 1 on 12-1-1981 and separate mutation Khatian No. 2034/4 holding No. 3903 in the name of purchaser Abdullah vide order of same date, paid land development tax to the Government.

11. Another registered partition deed No. 21974 dated 22-12-1982 was executed between the heirs of Jion Box in which entire aforesaid 0.78 acres was in the share of Sayedur Rahman, vendor of respondents. Being owner in his 0.15 acres land purchaser Abdullah gifted 0.15 acres to 4 sons of respondents No. 1-3 and Morshed Alam predecessor of respondents Nos. 4-6 and delivered possession. As such respondents have been possessing aforesaid 0.30 acres land. In last city survey aforesaid land of respondents were recorded in city survey plot No. 37161 with an area of 2924 Ojutangsha in draft Khatian No. 37111 in the name of respondents Nos. 1-3 and Morshed Alam predecessor of respondents Nos. 4-6. Later it was in their name in attested Khatian in 1999 and respondents got draft Khatian in their names. When printed Khatian published it was found that it was fraudulently printed in the name of present appellant Shamsul Alam and on query it was found that he managed to file objection case beyond knowledge of respondents and by suppression of process he managed to obtain order for record in his name behind the back of respondents. It was also found that appellant No. 3 managed to open mutation Khatian in his name for 0.20 acres land of SA plot No. 5159 corresponding RS plot No. 7460 on 25-4-2005 without serving any notice on respondents. Having scent of it, respondents filed Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2008 before Assistant Commissioner (Land) Demra for cancelling the said fraudulent Khatian published in the name of appellant which was ultimately allowed on contest.

12. That against wrong record of the case land in the name of appellant in City Survey, respondents filed land Survey Case No. 136 of 2008 against appellant before land Survey Tribunal, Dhaka and appellant filed written statement on 23-3-2009 where he disclosed that he mortgaged case land to Rupali Bank, local office, Dilkusha Branch. Then on query at that bank respondents found that their 0.20 acres land of SA plot No. 5159 corresponding RS plot No. 7460 was mortgaged by appellant to said bank though he was not owner of it and the bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 112 of 2007 against the appellant got decree on 7-4-2008, filed execution Case No. 13 of 2008 and 0.20 acres land of respondents was shown in serial No. 1 of `Kha' schedule of Execution Case. As 0.20 acres of these respondents were illegally mortgaged by title less appellant by practicing fraud on bank and land of respondents was illegally attached in said execution case. Respondents having no other alternative to but file Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 2009 before Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka with requisite bank guarantee under section 32 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 read with order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure for releasing their 0.20 acres land from attachment i.e. from auction sale. It is evident that respondent Nos. 1-6 filed the present miscellaneous case under section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat read with Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. At the time of filing of the application respondents deposited 10% of the decreetal amount and the present respondents submits security amount of Taka 9,91,500 equivalent to 10% of the decreetal money. Subsequently, by the impugned order dated 3-5-2012 miscellaneous case was allowed and accordingly the security amount was refunded to the respondent Nos. 1-6.

13. That the plaintiff-Bank, present respondent No. 7 and judgment-debtors 1-6 including present appellant contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing separate written objections.

14. In the present Miscellaneous Case, the Third-party-petitioner examined 5 PWs, 1 OPW on behalf of Bank and 4 OPWs including survey knowing Advocate Commissioner, Md Shamsul Hoque, who made local investigation of suit land deposed and documents filed by the parties were marked exhibits respectively, After hearing the parties court below found right, title and possession of applicant respondent Nos. 1-6 in case land and also found that judgment-debtor No. 2-present appellant has no right, title and possession in case land and, as such, allowed the Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 2009 and released 0'20 acres case land in favour of applicant, respondent Nos. 1-6 and also ordered to return guarantee given by applicants vide judgment and order dated 3-5-2012. Accordingly applicants of Miscellaneous Case applied for retuning the guarantee issued by Islami Bank Bangladesh, Head Office Branch, 40 Dilkusha Commercial area and their deposited documents and court below allowed said application of Third-party-claimant-applicants on 2-7-2012 and applicants withdrew their Bank guarantee and documents. Thus proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 2009 ended on 2-7-2012 i.e long before filing of the present appeal and no further proceeding was pending in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case and, as such, there is nothing to stay operation of impugned judgment and order dated 3-5-2012. It is stated that appellant illegally and falsely mortgaged lands including 0.20 acres land of these respondents to Rupali Bank and obtained loan and on his default in repayment. The respondent No. 7, Rupali Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 112 of 2007 against appellant and others and got decree on 7-4-2008, filed Money Execution Case No. 13 of 2008 as per provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain as 0.20 acres land of these respondents were illegally mortgaged by appellant to the plaintiff-Bank and execution case was started including attaching said 0.20 acres land of these respondents.

15. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the deeds of partition No. 2478 dated 9-3-1979 and 21974 dated 22-12-1982 did not contain the disputed CS Plot No. 5159, the learned judge erred in law in holding that the said plot was allotted to the saham of Sayedur Rahman, the predecessor-in-charge of the Third-party-claimant-respondent. He further submits that the learned judge failed to consider the evidence showing that the mortgaged land is located in the southern part of the disputed CS Plot No. 5159, whereas the third party claimant land is located in the northern part of the suit land. Learned Advocate by referring the provision of Section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 submits that the application was filed under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable since the third party failed to pay the statutory deposit, later on he did not press this submission. Learned Advocate for the judgment-debtor-appellant next submits that the learned Judge of the executing court committed gross error in allowing miscellaneous case admitting the fact that the court release the mortgage property measuring an area of 0.20 decimal out of 0.33 decimal and without partition the executing court cannot release the said property. Lastly, the learned Advocate strenuously argued that the appellant is not aggrieved by any order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, but filed the present appeal against the order passed by the learned Joint District in the miscellaneous case filed under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. So, the provision of sub-sections (2) of section 41(2) requiring a deposit of 50% of the decreetal amount as a pre-requisite for filing appeal against any order or decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat is not applicable in the present case. But the present appeal was filed invoking the provision of section 104 and order XLIII of the Code of Civil Procedure which have been made applicable under the said Ain.

16. At the time of delivery of judgment the learned Advocate for the appellant by referring section 40 and 41 of the Ain tried to argue that the term "order" in sub-section (1) of section 41 means "order" which favours "decree" or its "execution" the impugned order neither favours the decree nor its execution rather it hindrance execution of the decree in the sense that it excluded big portion of the mortgaged property measuring an area 0.20 acres out of attachment by releasing the property from attachment.

17. Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the Third-party-respondent Nos. 1-6 submits that by invoking the provision of section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain Third-party-petitioners-respondent Nos. 1-6 have filed the present miscellaneous case for releasing their 0'20 decimal land out of 0'33 acres of land of RS plot No. 7460 mentioned in the `KA' schedule to the plaint of Artha Rin Suit No. 112 of 2007 filed the respondent No. 7 Bank which was mortgaged to the bank by the defendant No.1 treating the same as their property. The learned Advocate mainly submits that the present appeal is not maintainable under section 41 rule (2) of the Ain, 2003. Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhury, Advocate in support of his submission in respect of maintainability of the appeal cited good number of decisions reported in 13 MLR (AD) 253, 16 DLR (SC) 287, 49 DLR (AD) 135 and 12 MLR (AD) 1 = 59 DLR (AD) 26.

18. Mr Imam Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.7-Bank by referring 41 of the Ain submits that the order passed by Artha Rin Adalat under section 13(2)(4) of the Ain and not order passed under section 32 of the Ain, so the statutory deposit under section 41 is not required in filing the present appeal. He further submits that the impugned order is not passed in Artha Rin Execution Case but. passed in Miscellaneous Case filed under section 32(2) read with Order XLI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

19. It appears that during the pendency of the Artha Rin Execution Case No. 14 of 2009 the judgment-debtor, present appellant filed Title Suit No. 193 of 2012 on 23-2-2012 before the Joint District Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka praying for a declaration and recovery of khan possession of the suit land against the present respondent Nos. 1-6 claiming that he was dispossessed from the suit by this defendant-respondent on 24-5-2010. The appellant suppressed about filing of the said suit both in the execution case and also in the present appeal. Respondent Nos. 1-6 have knowledge about the aforesaid suit, where they appeared and filed written statement on 17-2-2014. It further appears that the present appellant mutated the suit land by filing Mutation Case No. 4170 of 2005 having came to learn that appellant of present appeal filed Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2008 before the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Demra, Dhaka. After contesting hearing the mutated khatian in the name of the appellant was restored by order dated 27-4-2011. Subsequently, in Mohanagar Jarip the name of the appellant was wrongly recorded and against that respondent filed Land Survey Tribunal Case No. 136 of 2008 before the Land Survey Tribunal, Dhaka and same is now pending.

20. The moot question to be decided in the appeal whether the appeal filed by the judgment-debtor without depositing the statutory deposit as stipulated in section 41(2) of the Ain is maintainable or not.

21. It appears that the respondent Nos. 1-6 as third party filed Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 2009 on 23-6-2009 before the Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka under section 32 of the Ain, 2003 read with Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure with a statutory deposit of 10% of the decreetal amount of Taka 9,91,500. The said miscellaneous case was arises out of Artha Jari Case No. 13 of 2008 which was filed by the Decree-holder-plaintiff-Bank for executing the judgment and decree dated 30-3-2008 passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 112 of 2007.

22. In view of the above, we are left with no option but to decide whether the present appeal would lie without depositing of the 50% of the decreetal amount at the time of filing of the appeal under section 41 of the Ain, 2003. It appears that at the time of filing of the present appeal under section 41(1) of the Ain, the appellant did not comply with the requirement that is deposit of 50% of the decreetal amount. Rather the appellant subsequently filed an application on 16-7-2012 for dispensing the statutory deposit for filing the present appeal against the impugned order dated 3-5-2012 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. It is evident from the order dated 28-11-2012 that the appeal was admitted provisionally. It further appears that the memorandum of appeal being not enclosed with proof of deposit of 50% of decreetal amount and the filing of the appeal being subject to fulfillment of sub-section 2 of section 41 (উপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে), the filing of the memorandum of appeal simplicitor does not lead to hold that the appeal was entertainable legally.

23. Artha Rin Ain, 2003 is a special law and its provision had to be adhered to very strictly. Chapter VII of the Ain, 2003 dealt with the Appeal and Revision section 40 of the Ain speaks about the applicability of the relevant provision of the Code of Civil Procedure in respect of appeal and revision to be filed under Artha Rin Ain. Section 41 of the Ain has provided the procedure as to filing and disposal of the appeal against the decree or order of Artha Rin Ain, 2003. We considered, it would be convenient before proceeding further to reproduce the above two sections of the Ain, 2003 for proper understanding whether the appeal filed by the appellant was maintainable or not, the said section are as follows:

“৪০। দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধি আইনের প্রয়োগ-এই পরিচ্ছেদের অধীন আপীল ও রিভিশন কার্যক্রমে, এই আইনের বিধানাবলীর সহিত অসঙ্গতিপূর্ণ না হওয়া সাপেক্ষে, দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধি আইনের সংশ্লিষ্ট বিধানাবলী প্রযোজ্য হইবে ।

৪১। আপীল দায়ের ও নিষ্পত্তি সম্পর্কিত বিশেষ বিধান- (১) মামলার কোন পক্ষ, কোন অর্থ খণ আদালতের আদেশ বা ডিক্রি দ্বারা সংক্ষুব্ধ হইলে, যদি ডিক্রিকৃত টাকার পরিমাণ ৫০(পঞ্চাশ) লক্ষ টাকা অপেক্ষা অধিক হয়, তাহা হইলে উপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, (পরবর্তী ৬০ (ষাট) দিবসের] মধ্যে হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে, এবং যদি ডিক্রিকৃত টাকার পরিমাণ ৫০ (পঞ্চাশ) লক্ষ টাকা অখবা তদৃপেক্ষা কম হয়, [তাহা হইলে পরবর্তী ৩০ (ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে জেলা জজ আদালতে আপীল করিতে পারিবেন |]

(২) আপীলকারী, ডিক্রিকৃত টাকার পরিমাণের ৫০% এর সমপরিমাণ টাকা বাদীর দাবীর আংশিক স্বীকৃতিস্বরূপ নগদ ডিক্রিদার আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে, অথবা বাদীর দাবী স্বীকার না করিলে, জামানতম্বরূপ ডিক্রি প্রদানকারী আদালতে জমা করিয়া উক্তরূপ জমার প্রমাণ দরখাস্ত বা আপীলের মেমোর সহিত আদালতে দাখিল না করিলে, উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন কোন আপীল কার্যার্থে গৃহীত হইবে না।

(৩) উপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান সত্ত্বেও, বিবাদী-দায়িক ইতিমধ্যে ১৯(৩) ধারার বিধান মতে 90% দেশ শতাংশ) পরিমাণ নগদ অথবা জামানত হিসাবে জমা করিয়া থাকিলে, | অত্র ধারার অধীনে দায়েরের ক্ষেত্রে উক্ত ১০% (দশ শতাংশ) টাকা উপরি-উল্লিখিত ৫০% পেঞ্চাশ শতাংশ) টাকা হইতে বাদ হইবে।

(8) উপরি-উল্লিখিত বিধানাবলী সত্তেও বাদী-আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান এই ধারার অধীনে কোন আপীল দায়ের করিলে, উহাকে উপরি-উল্লিখিত মতে কোন টাকা বা জামানত জমাদান করিতে হইবে না।

(৫) জেলা জজ কোন আপীল গ্রহণ মাত্রই লিখিতভাবে উল্লেখ করিবেন যে, তিনি নিজেই উক্ত আপীল শুনানি করিবেন কিনা, এবং তিনি নিজে উক্ত আপীল শুনানি না করিতে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করিলে, অনতিবিলম্বে উক্ত আপীলটি শুনানির জন্য তাহার অধিক্ষেত্রের অধীন একজন অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজের নিকট, যদি থাকে, প্রেরণ করিবেন; এবং কোন অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ না থাকিলে, জেলা জজ নিজেই উক্ত আপীল শ্রবণ করিবেন।

(৬) আপীল আদালত, আপীল গৃহীত হইবার পরবর্তী ৯০ (নব্বই) দিবসের মধ্যে উহা নিষ্পত্তি করিবে, এবং ৯০ (নব্বই) দিবসের মধ্যে আপীলটি নিষ্পত্তি করিতে ব্যর্থ হইলে, আদালত, লিখিতভাবে কারণ উল্লেখপূর্বক, উক্ত সময়সীমা অনধিক আরো ৩০ (ত্রিশ) দিবস বর্ধিত করিতে পারিবে ।”

24. From a reading of section 40 of the Ain, 2003 it is apparent that the provision of appeal and revision of the Code of Civil Procedure such as sections 96 and 104, Order XLI and XLIII and section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure have been made applicable in respect of appeal and a revision filed under the said Ain. Here we are concerned with the appeal, as there is no dispute that the present miscellaneous appeal was filed by the judgment-debtor-appellant under section 41 of the Ain, 2003.

<u>25. On perusal of section 41 of the Ain, 2003 it appears that appeal would lie to the High Court Division against any order or decree passed by Artha Rin Adalat within 60 days subject to fulfillment of condition mentioned therein, that is deposit of 50% of the decreetal amount and submit with the memorandum of appeal the proof of such deposit and it has further been provided that in the absence of submitting such proof with memorandum of appeal no appeal filed under sub-section (1) of section 41 shall be accepted for any action. In sub-section (1) of section 41 the period of filing an appeal has been mentioned and it has also been mentioned that such appeal is to be filed subject to sub-section (2) of section 41 of the Ain ((9t-sM1 () fdkft ftcverm) prescribing, as we have already noticed, the requirement of submission of proof of deposit of 50% of the decreetal amount. If the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 41 and sub-section (2) of the said section are read meticulously it shall be crystal clear that filing of appeal under sub-section (1) is subject to fulfillment of the requirement of sub-section (2) of the Ain and both the provisions are therefore conjunctive and not disjunctive at all. Reading section 41 along with section 40 of the Ain, 2003 it further appears to us that the provisions of the Code will be applicable so far as the proceeding in filing the appeal.</u>

26. It appears from the record that the Memorandum of Appeal from original order was filed on 16-7-2012 which was registered as First Miscellaneous Appeal Tender No. 596 of 2012 being not accompanied with 50% of the decreetal amount. On 28-11-2012 First Miscellaneous Appeal Tendered (FMAT) No. 596 of 2012 appeared in the daily cause list not under Order XLI, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for admission hearing but under the heading for hearing only. Learned Judge of the Division Bench provisionally admitted the appeal by order dated 28-11-2012.

27. Thus it is crystal clear grievance made by the third party respondent Nos. 1-6 in the present miscellaneous appeal arises out of the decree passed in Artha Rin Mamla No. 112 of 2007 and Artha Jari Case No. 13 of 2008. Thus we find no substance in the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the appellant.

<u>28. As there is a mandatory provision to deposit 50% of the decreetal amount to prefer appeal, the present appeal is not at all maintainable and in fact there is no appeal in the eye of law. It further appears from the record that in the absence of 50% of the decreetal amount deposit to prefer appeal there is no existence of appeal in the eye of law. In this connection we can easily rely on the decision reported in 13 MLR (AD) 253.</u>

29. In the miscellaneous case the Third-party-petitioner-respondent Nos. 1-6 examined 5 PWs, on the other hand appellant-opposite party examined 4 OPWs. In the miscellaneous case local investigation was held and the advocate Commissioner who conducted the local investigation was also examined in this proceeding as OPW 4. The court after considering the evidence and materials on record rightly passed order for releasing the property from attachment to the extent of 0.20 decimal southern part of SA Plot No. 5159 corresponding RS Plot No. 7460 out of total area of 0.33 acres land and plaintiff claimed only 0'20 acres southern part.

30. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, relevant provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, Code of Civil Procedure and the decisions of our apex court, we find no substance in the submissions of the learned advocate for the appellant. As there is the mandatory provision to deposit 50% of the decreetal amount to prefer appeal, the instant appeal is not at all maintainable.

31. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

32. Consequently, the connected Civil Rule No. 78(FM) of 2013 is discharged.

Let a copy of the judgment be sent to the concerned court expeditiously.
